nodes.goal: The larger requests from rc1 adopters: promote carries the converge judgement into the graph, batch input, structured placement, decisions, repo evidence and scriptable graph editing.
nodes.title: Brainstorm and roadmap editing features

acceptance: The sheet's References list overlaps with existing nodes by id and relation; Approach lists the critics' objections and the verdict reasoning as constraints
The anchor's sheet gains a 'Brainstorm frame' section with the recorded frame
promote writes work/brainstorm-<slug>-authoring-prompt.md asking an agent to draft Approach, Tasks, acceptance, touch zones and references per promoted node from the session
Existing promote tests still pass; new tests cover each section
nodes.goal: A promoted node's sheet holds what the brainstorm learned about it, and the batch comes with a prompt that fills the rest.
nodes.title: promote carries the converge judgement into sheets and writes an authoring prompt

acceptance: `revise --target-parent <ID>` is honoured by promote; ideas without one use --under
`promote --by-cluster` creates one node per cluster lead and lists the others as alternatives
`promote --min-recommendation strong` skips weaker verdicts
`promote --plan plan.yaml` creates a tree (parent, type, title, acceptance, dependencies by display id) and links ideas by id
nodes.goal: Accepted ideas land where the PM intends in one command.
nodes.title: Structured promote: target parents, clusters, minimum recommendation, plan file

acceptance: `add-idea --from-file ideas.yaml` (or JSONL on stdin) records all ideas or none, with the existing flag names as keys
`revise --from-file verdicts.yaml` applies all verdicts or none
`brainstorm merge <ID> --into <IDs>` sets status merged with reverse links; promote skips merged ideas
`add-idea --from-gap` marks an idea as raised in the converge pass and recommend lists it for a verdict
`brainstorm cluster <CID> --name ... --best <ID> --critic ...` records the cluster as an object shown by `list --by cluster`
nodes.goal: Sixty ideas or verdicts are one command and one transaction, duplicates merge instead of being rejected, and gap ideas have a sanctioned origin.
nodes.title: Batch ideas and verdicts from a file, merge, and gap ideas

acceptance: `--kind policy` exists; `brainstorm decide <ID> --decision ...` sets status decided
promote renders decided ideas into the anchor's sheet as a 'Decided policies' section instead of nodes
`frame --amend KEY --answer ...` keeps the previous answer in history; `frame --provisional` and `--confirm` mark the frame and later prompts show the state
nodes.goal: A decision made during a brainstorm is recorded as a decision, not as a parked or rejected idea, and the frame can change with history.
nodes.title: Policies and decisions as first-class brainstorm outcomes; frame amendments

acceptance: `add-evidence --source-type repo --path file:line` records the commit and verify checks the quote against that commit locally
`add-evidence --query ... --no-result` records a disconfirming search with no hit
`add-idea --evidence URL --quote ...` records a verifiable source
nodes.goal: Brownfield brainstorms can cite code and record a search that found nothing.
nodes.title: Repository files as evidence; null results; quotes on research-born ideas

acceptance: Persona and direction text in prompts is derived from the recorded `served` answer, with `--profile personal` as a lens set for single-author tools
The recommend prompt lists phases plus the nodes most similar to the ideas (via the search index) instead of every node
nodes.goal: Personas fit the product being brainstormed and the recommend prompt stays readable on a large roadmap.
nodes.title: Lenses from the frame and a ranked node list in the recommend prompt

acceptance: `specy-road apply changes.yaml --dry-run` validates the whole batch (add-node, edit-node, add-dependency entries) and prints the resulting ready/blocked waves without writing
Without --dry-run the batch is applied atomically or not at all
`add-node --acceptance` is repeatable; `--dependency` and `add-dependency` accept display ids and store node_keys
nodes.goal: A large roadmap change can be rehearsed and applied as one validated batch.
nodes.title: Scriptable graph edits: apply a change file with dry run, acceptance at creation, display-id dependencies

acceptance: `list-nodes --json` emits the full node list without title truncation
`refresh-stubs --diff` shows the managed-block and skill changes before writing
move-node rewrites touch-zone path segments that equal the old display id
`finish-this-task` in merge mode can delete the merged feature branch locally and on the remote (`--delete-branch`), and `specy-road branches prune` lists or deletes merged feature/rm-* branches
nodes.goal: Listing is scriptable, stub refreshes are previewable, and renumbering does not strand touch zones.
nodes.title: list-nodes --json, refresh-stubs --diff, move-node zone rewrite

acceptance: `do-next-available-task --prefer-agentic` (and a git-workflow.yaml default) orders Agentic-led before Mixed before Human-led within the same tree position
grind-session --plan prints the execution milestone next to the next auto-pick
nodes.goal: An unattended loop can prefer Agentic-led leaves without changing the default order.
nodes.title: Opt-in auto-pick ordering by execution milestone
